claim: In NIST's definition an APT pursues its objective repeatedly over an extended period and adapts to the defender's resistance.
quote: The advanced persistent threat: (i) pursues its objectives repeatedly over an extended period of time; (ii) adapts to defenders’ efforts to resist it; and (iii) is determined to maintain the level of interaction needed to execute its objectives.
locator: p. B-1 printed (PDF p. 60), Appendix B Glossary
issue: Same definition in footnote 82 (PDF p. 88). The dissertation files both under 'persistent'; NIST does not split the definition by word, but the sentence only attributes the content.

claim: An APT's objectives are data exfiltration, impediment of mission-critical components, or positioning for future operations.
quote: These objectives typically include establishing and extending footholds within the information technology infrastructure of the targeted organizations for purposes of exfiltrating information, undermining or impeding critical aspects of a mission, program, or organization; or positioning itself to carry out these objectives in the future.
locator: p. B-1 printed (PDF p. 60), Appendix B Glossary
issue: Adversarial reading: NIST says the objectives 'typically include' these three, and the impediment is of 'critical aspects of a mission, program, or organization', not 'components'; the sentence's 'defined by its objective' closes the list. Paraphrase within tolerance.

claim: The APT definition gives campaign persistence (pursues its objective over an extended period) and adaptivity (adapts to the defender's resistance).
quote: The advanced persistent threat: (i) pursues its objectives repeatedly over an extended period of time; (ii) adapts to defenders’ efforts to resist it; and (iii) is determined to maintain the level of interaction needed to execute its objectives.
locator: p. B-1 printed (PDF p. 60), Appendix B Glossary
issue: Objective-specific behaviour and detection avoidance are not in NIST's definition; they rest on co-cite alshamrani2019 (checked: supported).

claim: Campaign persistence: pursues its objective over an extended period.
quote: The advanced persistent threat: (i) pursues its objectives repeatedly over an extended period of time; (ii) adapts to defenders’ efforts to resist it; and (iii) is determined to maintain the level of interaction needed to execute its objectives.
locator: p. B-1 printed (PDF p. 60), Appendix B Glossary
issue: 'One multi-stage campaign' is not NIST's; it rests on co-cite alshamrani2019.

claim: Adaptivity: chooses its next technique in response to an MTD disruption.
quote: The advanced persistent threat: (i) pursues its objectives repeatedly over an extended period of time; (ii) adapts to defenders’ efforts to resist it; and (iii) is determined to maintain the level of interaction needed to execute its objectives.
locator: p. B-1 printed (PDF p. 60), Appendix B Glossary
issue: NIST says only that an APT 'adapts to defenders’ efforts to resist it'. Choosing the next technique, and MTD disruption as the resistance, are the dissertation's operationalisation, carried (if at all) by co-cite cho2020 (not checked here). Fine as a pair; NIST alone supports the general property.
